title: Gross income and filing status — Jordan Reyes
instructions: Jordan Reyes, divorced in 2016, lives with her 12-year-old son, who lived with her all year; she paid all costs of their home. Classify each 2025 item and compute her gross income.

exhibits.title: 2025 receipts
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Wages | 68,000 |
| Employer-paid health insurance premiums | 7,200 |
| Employer-provided group-term life insurance ($40,000 of coverage) — cost | 180 |
| Interest on City of Austin bonds | 1,500 |
| Interest on corporate bonds | 900 |
| State income tax refund (she itemized in 2024; the deduction reduced her tax in full) | 600 |
| Inheritance from her aunt | 25,000 |
| Gambling winnings | 2,000 |
| Alimony received under the 2016 divorce decree | 12,000 |
| Child support received | 6,000 |
| Jury duty pay | 300 |

parts.prompt: Included in or excluded from gross income?

rows.label: State income tax refund
rows.explanation: Tax benefit rule — the prior deduction reduced tax.

rows.label: Alimony under the 2016 decree
rows.explanation: Pre-2019 instruments: alimony remains income (unless modified to adopt the new rules).

rows.label: Jordan's filing status
rows.explanation: Unmarried, paid all costs of a home for a qualifying child who lived with her all year.

rows.label: Her son is her
rows.explanation: Relationship, age, residency, and support tests are met.

reviewNote: Relies on 2025 amounts set by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (standard deduction, child tax credit, or SALT cap). Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.
